description: RabbitMQ (dt-broker): pod health, message flow and resource limits
title: RabbitMQ Health Monitoring

panels.title: Pods ready
panels.description: How many RabbitMQ pods are running and ready. We run 3. Green = 3, orange = 2 (still works), red = 1 or 0 (cluster is down).

panels.title: Nodes sending metrics
panels.description: How many RabbitMQ nodes Prometheus can read data from. Should match Pods ready. Lower means RabbitMQ inside a pod is stuck.

panels.title: Active alarms
panels.description: Memory, disk or connection-limit alarms. Must be 0. Any alarm means RabbitMQ has STOPPED accepting new messages.

panels.title: Pod restarts
panels.description: How many times RabbitMQ pods restarted in the selected time range. Should be 0.

panels.title: Messages waiting
panels.description: Messages sitting in queues, not yet picked up (the backlog). Orange from 1,000, red from 10,000.

panels.title: Messages in progress
panels.description: Messages a consumer has picked up but not yet confirmed (unacked). A high number means consumers are slow or stuck.

panels.title: Consumers
panels.description: Number of app listeners reading from queues. 0 means nobody is processing messages.

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Number of apps connected to RabbitMQ right now.

panels.title: Pods: status of each RabbitMQ pod
Pod status
panels.description: One row per RabbitMQ pod. Ready = Kubernetes health check passes. Metrics = Prometheus can read it. Restarts = in selected time range. Alarms must be 0.

targets.expr: max by (pod) (rabbitmq_alarms_memory_used_watermark{namespace=~"$namespace",pod=~"$pod"}) + max by (pod) (rabbitmq_alarms_free_disk_space_watermark{namespace=~"$namespace",pod=~"$pod"}) + max by (pod) (rabbitmq_alarms_file_descriptor_limit{namespace=~"$namespace",pod=~"$pod"})

panels.title: Pod ready over time
panels.description: Green = pod was ready, red = pod was not ready. Use it to see when an outage started and ended.

panels.title: CPU used
panels.description: CPU cores used by each RabbitMQ pod. The dashed line is the limit (2 cores).

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: Memory used by each RabbitMQ pod. The dashed line is the limit (4 GiB). Kubernetes kills the pod if it goes over.

panels.title: Queues
panels.description: All queues combined, per RabbitMQ pod (each queue is counted on the pod that hosts it). Ready = waiting to be picked up. Unacked = picked up, not yet confirmed. Total = Ready + Unacked. Consumers = app listeners connected to that pod.

panels.title: Messages ready by pod
panels.description: Messages waiting to be picked up, per pod. Dashed lines: orange = 1,000 (warning alert), red = 10,000 (critical alert).

panels.title: Messages unacked by pod
panels.description: Messages picked up by a consumer but not yet confirmed, per pod. A growing line means consumers are slow or stuck.

panels.title: Messages in vs out (per second)
panels.description: In = messages published to RabbitMQ. Out = messages delivered to consumers. If In stays above Out, the backlog grows.

panels.title: Consumers, connections and queues
panels.description: Consumers = app listeners. Connections = apps connected. Queues = number of queues. Sudden drops to 0 mean apps lost their connection.

panels.title: Lost messages (unroutable)
panels.description: Messages sent to RabbitMQ that matched no queue, so they were dropped or sent back. Should be 0. Usually a wrong routing key or a missing queue.

panels.title: Limits: how close is RabbitMQ to blocking?
Memory vs RabbitMQ limit
panels.description: Memory used as % of RabbitMQ's own limit (60% of pod memory). At 100% RabbitMQ raises an alarm and blocks publishers. Alert at 85%.

panels.title: Disk space used
panels.description: How full each RabbitMQ data disk (20 GiB) is. RabbitMQ blocks publishers when free space drops below about 8 GiB. Alert at 80%.

panels.title: Connection and process limits
panels.description: File handles = open connections and files, as % of the OS limit. Erlang processes = RabbitMQ's internal tasks, as % of its limit. At 100% new connections are refused. Alert at 80%.
